intent: An adult new to the domain, here to build a working mental model, not to make an immediate decision.
domain_familiarity: New to the domain; no prior exposure to its vocabulary or standard methods assumed.
purpose: Wants to build a working mental model of the domain, step by step, that later material can build on.
assumed_knowledge: no prior exposure to the domain's vocabulary, methods, or standard debates

text.explanation_depth: define every term on first use; build concepts in dependency order rather than assuming any can be skipped
text.section_granularity: short sections with an explicit recap linking back to the previous one

visual.label_density: low; one concept introduced per visual
visual.legend: always shown and explained, not just present
visual.acronym_expansion: expand every acronym, and repeat the expansion the first few times it recurs

audio.pace: slower than the default conversational pace
audio.term_glossing: every term glossed on first use
audio.useful_recurrence: higher than any other adult audience; key terms and structure are repeated across the piece to reinforce the model being built

anti_patterns: Assuming any prior vocabulary or method familiarity
Introducing more than one genuinely new concept per unit of explanation
Rushing pace or cutting recap to fit a time or length budget
Treating the beginner-learner adult audience as equivalent to a child audience — vocabulary ceiling and reasoning mode differ; see audience/child-upper-elementary.json for the child-specific profile
